metadata.title: Vertex Cover: Why Twice Optimal Is a Promise

beats.new_visual_element: ROLE HOOK · BrutalistHesitantWriter; silent mystery, zero static card.

props.text:
This greedy cover wastes a vertex.
So how can it still promise
twice optimal?

beats.narration_text: On this four-leaf star, one center vertex covers every edge. Now choose any edge and take both endpoints. We return two vertices where optimum needs one.
beats.tts_normalized_text: On this four leaf star, one center vertex covers every edge. Now choose any edge and take both endpoints. We return two vertices where optimum needs one.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE INSTANCE 1 · Star trace shows algorithm two versus optimum one.

beats.narration_text: Try a four-vertex path. Choose the middle edge, take both endpoints, and every edge disappears. This time two vertices are also optimal.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Try a four vertex path. Choose the middle edge, take both endpoints, and every edge disappears. This time two vertices are also optimal.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE INSTANCE 2 · Path trace returns an exact cover of two.

beats.narration_text: The same rule was exact once and twice optimal once. Before the proof, predict what property the edges chosen by the algorithm must share.
beats.tts_normalized_text: The same rule was exact once and twice optimal once. Before the proof, predict what property the edges chosen by the algorithm must share.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE PREDICT · Two outcomes hold while question writes over yellow fill.

beats.narration_text: Run the star again. After choosing one edge, deleting every incident edge leaves nothing. On a larger graph, every later chosen edge is disjoint from the earlier ones.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Run the star again. After choosing one edge, deleting every incident edge leaves nothing. On a larger graph, every later chosen edge is disjoint from the earlier ones.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE TRACE / TRANSFORM · Incident edges vanish; disjoint chosen edges persist.

beats.narration_text: Each chosen edge forces every possible cover to include at least one of its endpoints. Because chosen edges share no endpoints, those payments cannot be reused.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Each chosen edge forces every possible cover to include at least one of its endpoints. Because chosen edges share no endpoints, those payments cannot be reused.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE INSTANCE / CERTIFICATE · Three disjoint edges drive a one-per-edge lower-bound ledger.

beats.narration_text: That is the license: the chosen edges form a maximal matching, and their disjointness is a lower-bound certificate. The algorithm pays two vertices for every one vertex optimum must pay.
beats.tts_normalized_text: That is the license: the chosen edges form a maximal matching, and their disjointness is a lower bound certificate. The algorithm pays two vertices for every one vertex optimum must pay.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE ABSTRACTION · Characteristics maximal matching and disjoint lower-bound certificate named after instances.

beats.narration_text: Back at the star, the algorithm’s two vertices look wasteful, but the selected edge certifies optimum cannot use zero. Two is therefore the worst permitted multiple, not a guess.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Back at the star, the algorithm's two vertices look wasteful, but the selected edge certifies optimum cannot use zero. Two is therefore the worst permitted multiple, not a guess.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE PAYOFF · Same hook star returns with numeric two-for-one ledger.

beats.narration_text: The verdict: approximation replaces an unreachable exact promise with a checkable bound. Disjoint chosen edges certify the lower bound; taking both endpoints certifies coverage.
beats.tts_normalized_text: The verdict: approximation replaces an unreachable exact promise with a checkable bound. Disjoint chosen edges certify the lower bound; taking both endpoints certifies coverage.
